newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says Serbian crisis an internal affair.
newsitem.headline: Russia says Serbian crisis an internal affair.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said on Monday the dispute between President Slobodan Milosevic and the opposition was an internal matter for Serbia and warned other states not to interfere.

"I regard events in Belgrade as an internal matter for Yugoslavia. Of course all problems of human rights, of democratisation of any society worry us, but that must not develop into interference in the internal affairs of another state," Primakov told a news conference.

Belgrade and some other Serbian towns have been hit by a series of protests and demonstrations over the past three weeks in which students and opposition supporters have demanded that Milosevic own up to alleged vote-rigging in local elections.
Western powers, led by Washiungton, have also stepped up criticism of the Serbian leader's autocratic rule.

"We should use existing legal means to influence the situation without crossing the line to the point which could create inconveniences or serious difficulties for the contuinuation of the peace process," Primakov said in answer to a question.
He said Milosevic deserved credit for having offered to hold talks with the opposition -- an offer the opposition had declined -- and of the fact that no blood had been shed.

"I think the world community should take account of this step by Milosevic and of the fact that force has not been used, and of the fact that he opened all mass media which were temporarily switched off," Primakov said.

He said Russia had supported the recent mission to Belgrade led by Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini after which Yugoslavia invited the OSCE -- the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe -- to help resolve the crisis.
Russia has traditionally had close ties with its fellow Orthodox Christian Slavs in Serbia.
